boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Regimental rituals that mark the Academy’s transition from candidate to cadet, from daily formation to the waterfront sendoff.

cards.title: Two Weeks of Orientation
cards.subtitle: Academy-wide candidate training tradition
cards.notes: Follow the official Orientation schedule to understand the Academy’s two-week entry ritual, from opening ceremony through graduation and the mini cruise.
cards.short_summary: The Academy’s formal transition into regimental life begins with an intensive, structured Orientation program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy describes Orientation as a two-week program that immerses cadet candidates in its maritime customs and traditions.
cards.access_notes: Participation is for incoming cadet candidates; consult the official schedule for public ceremony details.

cards.title: Meet the Cadre
cards.subtitle: Orientation’s company leadership introduction
cards.notes: Look for the company introduction during Orientation, when candidates meet the cadre members who will lead and support their training.
cards.short_summary: Each company formally meets its Orientation leadership team in this long-standing Academy ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy’s Orientation site calls Meet the Cadre a long-standing tradition in which each company is introduced to its leadership team.
cards.access_notes: This is part of the incoming-candidate Orientation program.

cards.title: The 7:20 Morning Formation
cards.subtitle: Parade Field weekday muster
cards.notes: Watch the Parade Field webcam on a weekday morning to see cadets muster and salute the American flag at the scheduled formation.
cards.short_summary: A weekday Parade Field muster gives the Regiment a highly visible daily rhythm.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says cadets muster to salute the American flag every morning Monday through Friday at 0720.
cards.access_notes: The Academy provides a Parade Field webcam; in-person viewing should respect campus access rules.

cards.title: Uniform of the Day
cards.subtitle: The Academy’s shared daily dress practice
cards.notes: Notice the classroom-black uniform in academic spaces and ceremonies; the Academy frames the Uniform of the Day as a tradition of solidarity.
cards.short_summary: Cadets’ required Uniform of the Day turns everyday classes and meals into a regimental ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that complete Uniform of the Day is required and that its uniforms represent an Academy tradition of solidarity.
cards.access_notes: Cadets are required to follow the Academy’s uniform standards; visitors should not enter restricted spaces.

cards.title: Standing for Taps
cards.subtitle: Orientation’s nightly closing observance
cards.notes: During Orientation, recognize the nightly closing procedure from a respectful distance; it is an Academy observance rather than a visitor activity.
cards.short_summary: The playing of Taps closes Orientation days and sends cadet candidates to bed.
cards.evidence_claim: An official Orientation account says cadet candidates stood at attention for Taps and describes it as a military procedure honoring those who served.
cards.access_notes: This occurs within Orientation and is not presented as a public participation event.

cards.title: Patio Knowledge Recitation
cards.subtitle: Company knowledge check during Orientation
cards.notes: Read the official Orientation account before visiting: patio sessions have candidates answer Youngie Knowledge questions together before regimental staff.
cards.short_summary: Candidates demonstrate shared Academy knowledge aloud during the recurring patio session.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy reports that companies are brought before Regimental Staff at patio and expected to recite Youngie Knowledge in unison.
cards.access_notes: A supervised Orientation practice for cadet candidates; do not interrupt sessions.

cards.title: The Moonbeam at the Mess Deck
cards.subtitle: Orientation table-setting custom
cards.notes: Treat this as a documented Orientation custom: candidates place a flashlight, called a moonbeam, before them while learning Mess Deck procedures.
cards.short_summary: A flashlight becomes a named part of the candidate dining routine during Orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: An official Orientation account instructs cadet candidates to take out their “moonbeam” flashlight and place it in front of them at the table.
cards.access_notes: This custom is taught to Orientation candidates in the Mess Deck; dining access is governed by Academy rules.

cards.title: The Orientation Mini Cruise
cards.subtitle: Candidate voyage aboard the Patriot State
cards.notes: Follow official ship-tracking and Orientation updates for the candidate voyage, which travels from Buzzards Bay through Long Island Sound and New York City.
cards.short_summary: The Orientation calendar includes a multi-day Patriot State voyage before candidates complete the first training phase.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy schedules an Orientation Mini Cruise and publishes its route from Buzzards Bay through Long Island Sound, New York City, and back.
cards.access_notes: The voyage is for Orientation participants; use official ship tracking rather than attempting dock access.

cards.title: Orientation Graduation
cards.subtitle: Completion of the first training phase
cards.notes: Check the official Orientation calendar for the ceremony time and family information; it marks completion of the first phase of Academy training.
cards.short_summary: Candidates formally complete basic Orientation training before beginning the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that Orientation Graduation marks completion of phase 1, its basic-training phase.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists family-oriented graduation programming; times are subject to change.

cards.title: The Cadet Recognition Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The moment candidates become officially recognized cadets
cards.notes: Consult the Academy’s current Orientation page for date and attendance information; this later ceremony recognizes proficiency in the second training phase.
cards.short_summary: Recognition is the formal milestone separating candidates from officially recognized Academy cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says the Recognition Ceremony celebrates completion of phase 2 and signifies candidates are proficient enough to be officially recognized as cadets.
cards.access_notes: The Academy’s official Orientation page lists the ceremony; verify scheduling before travel.
